lines.text: An OpMode is one way the robot can run. Teleop is one of them, and each one is its own class.
The project creator already made a teleop for you. The annotation at the top is what puts it on the driver station.
So edit that file. Don't add a second one, or you'll end up with two teleops on the list.
Clear out the empty methods, and bind the buttons in the constructor. The robot hands it the arm and the flywheel.
Every button has two edges. Pressing it is one, letting go is the other, and each edge gets its own binding.
Hold the left trigger, and the arm pushes. Let go, and the release runs stop.
The right trigger's release is different. It drops the flywheel back to three volts, not to zero.
Your turn. Choose what the release does, then let go.
Bindings belong to their mode. Switch to auto, and the triggers do nothing. Switch back, and they're there again. There's nothing to clean up.
Every hold needs a release. Next, you'll see exactly what happens without one.
